questions.q: What is the Pub/Sub API primarily designed for?
options: Replacing Apex triggers entirely inside Salesforce
Only reading custom object records via SOQL
External, non-Salesforce clients that need to publish and subscribe to platform events, CDC events, and other event types
Replacing the lightning/empApi module inside Lightning Web Components
questions.explain: Pub/Sub API is aimed primarily at external clients outside Salesforce; inside an LWC, lightning/empApi remains the right tool since it already wraps the equivalent connection.

questions.q: What underlying technologies is Pub/Sub API built on, as opposed to the Bayeux/CometD model?
options: SOAP over HTTP/1.0
GraphQL over WebSockets
Plain REST with JSON payloads
gRPC over HTTP/2, with Avro-encoded payloads
questions.explain: Pub/Sub API is built on gRPC and HTTP/2, with event payloads encoded in Avro — a different technical foundation than CometD's Bayeux-based long polling.

questions.q: Which capabilities does a single Pub/Sub API client unify into one API, compared to a traditional CometD client?
options: Only subscribing — publishing still requires a separate API
Only schema discovery — publishing and subscribing still need separate connections
Only Change Data Capture events, never custom platform events
Publishing, subscribing, and requesting schema/topic information all in one API
questions.explain: Pub/Sub API consolidates publishing, subscribing, and schema/topic discovery into one coherent API, removing the need for separate mechanisms a custom CometD client would otherwise require.

questions.q: A Pub/Sub API client needs to uniquely identify a specific event message for deduplication purposes. Which field does it check?
options: EventUuid, exactly like a CometD client
The Replay ID, treated as a durable unique key
entityName from the ChangeEventHeader
The event's own `id` field, since Pub/Sub API clients don't have an EventUuid field
questions.explain: Pub/Sub API clients don't see an EventUuid field; the same UUID value is carried in the event's own id field instead.

questions.q: Inside a Lightning Web Component, which should you use to subscribe to a platform event — lightning/empApi or a hand-built Pub/Sub API client?
options: A hand-built Pub/Sub API client, since empApi is deprecated
Neither; LWCs cannot subscribe to platform events
Both are required together for every LWC subscriber
lightning/empApi, since it already wraps the equivalent streaming connection and there's no reason to hand-roll a gRPC client inside Salesforce's own UI layer
questions.explain: lightning/empApi already provides subscribe/unsubscribe functionality for an LWC. Pub/Sub API is the right tool for external, non-Salesforce clients, not for code running inside Salesforce's own UI layer.
